small_guidance:
- Add a GROUP_M block-swizzle (e.g. 8) to the GEMM for better L2 reuse across N tiles in a row group; with M=N=1024 (wait, M=1024, N=8192) this matters significantly for the wide-N case.
- Expand autotune to include larger K tiles (BLOCK_K=64, 128) with num_stages=4 since K=8192 is very large; the K loop currently dominates and deeper pipelining will overlap loads better. Try `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=4`.
- Fuse the softmax with the GEMM epilogue when N fits in a single program: emit one program per M-row that computes the full row of GEMM+BN+scale into registers/SRAM, then does max/exp/sum/normalize before storing — eliminates the 2 extra passes over a 1024×8192 tensor.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a single persistent fused kernel: one program per output row computes the entire GEMM row (looping over K in BLOCK_K chunks across all N tiles), applies BN+scale fused mul/shift, performs online softmax (running max + running sum with correction), then writes the normalized row. This collapses the kernel count from 2 to 1 and avoids materializing the 1024×8192 logits to HBM.
- Alternatively, split-K GEMM: with K=8192 and M=1024, N=8192, a split-K reduction (atomic-add or two-stage) can saturate SMs better than the current 2D grid; combine with a separate fused BN+softmax kernel that does online softmax in one pass.
- Consider tf32 (`tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)`) or storing W transposed once at init so the K-axis load on W is contiguous, removing strided loads in the hot loop.
